source.data: Darwinism. First published Fri Aug 13, 2004. Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species in November 1859, presenting a theory of descent with modification by means of natural selection. In his Autobiography Darwin recalls that in October 1838 he happened to read Malthus on Population for amusement, and that it at once struck him that favourable variations would tend to be preserved. Historians have long debated how much the Origin owes to Malthus; some argue that the essay supplied the key insight, while others hold that Darwin's reading of the animal breeders mattered more.
